facts.label: Perguntas no present perfect com anyone e everyone
facts.sub: Anyone, someone e everyone usam has: Has anyone seen it? Everyone has left. Para você ou eles, use Have you / Have they + particípio.

facts.label: Alguém…?
facts.sub: Use Has anyone + particípio para perguntar a um grupo: Has anyone seen my keys? Has anyone called? Anyone usa has, como he e she.

facts.label: Todo mundo
facts.sub: Use everyone com has: Everyone has left. Everyone has lost something once. Mesmo que pareça plural, o verbo fica no singular.

compare.br: No Brasil, perguntamos “alguém viu?” com o verbo no passado.
compare.us: Em inglês, use Has anyone + particípio? e Have you + particípio? Anyone, someone e everyone pedem has, não have.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Anyone is common in questions and negatives.
Someone is common in positive sentences.

items.why: We say Has anyone seen it?

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Anyone is common in questions and negatives. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Someone is common in positive sentences. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Have anyone seen it?” → Falso (We say Has anyone seen it?)

pages.title: A bright Austin kitchen · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hurried morning in a bright kitchen in Austin. Toast pops up and the radio plays loud music. Felix opens every drawer and checks each pocket. His wallet is on the table, but his keys are gone. His friend Ana sits with a cup of tea. She watches him walk in circles.

“Has anyone seen my keys? I’ve looked everywhere.” says Felix. “Have you checked your jacket? Everyone has lost keys in a jacket once.” says Ana. “Yes, I have. Has someone moved them from the table?” says Felix.
